Accruals and deferrals

Puts each cost and each income item in the month it belongs to: accrues what was used but not yet billed, defers what was paid in advance, and checks last month's reversals.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, the September 2026 close. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin accruals and deferrals skill

Can you do our September accruals and deferrals?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need nine answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one. The last two are optional.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
  2. Which company?
  3. Which period? Please give the exact start and end dates.
  4. Which categories are in scope: compensation, interest, utilities and services, revenue, deferred revenue, professional fees or tax?
  5. What supports each category? I need the facts that the books cannot show, such as the bonus estimate, loan terms, contract periods and fee letters.
  6. Do accruals reverse on day one of the next month, or does the next bill post against the accrual?
  7. Do you keep the books on the accrual basis or the cash basis?
  8. Optional: which materiality threshold do you use? I never choose one for you.
  9. Optional: which reporting framework and which tax country apply?

Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading, 1 to 30 September. Bonus, interest, utilities, audit fees and deferred revenue. Our managing director estimates the 2026 bonus at $240,000. Payroll tax is 8%. The auditor says 75% of the $12,000 audit is done. Accruals reverse on day one. Accrual basis. Materiality is $500. US GAAP and US tax.

Claude

Here is my plan for Northbrook Trading, 1 to 30 September, on the accrual basis. Your books are in US dollars with a calendar year, so September is month 9 of the bonus year. In scope are the bonus, interest on the term loan, utilities, audit fees and deferred revenue. Materiality is $500.

Electricity and audit fees reverse on 1 October. The bonus, its payroll tax and the interest build up month by month, so they do not reverse. Deferred items go to your Deferred revenue account. For accruals, your chart has two accounts: Accrued expenses and Accrued liabilities – other. Which one do I use? And shall I start?

Use Accrued expenses. Yes, go ahead.

Claude

I found five accruals for September. Each one has a basis that you or the books gave me:

September accruals
Bonus, 240,000 × 9 ÷ 12, less $160,000 already accrued$20,000.00
+ Employer payroll tax on the bonus, 8%$1,600.00
+ Interest on the $300,000 loan, 15 days at 6.5%$801.37
+ Electricity, 30 days at $70.00 a day (2,170 ÷ 31)$2,100.00
+ Audit fees, 75% of $12,000$9,000.00
= Accruals for September$33,501.37

For interest, I used the loan's own day count, actual/365. Actual/360 gives $812.50. Electricity and audit fees reverse on 1 October, a total of $11,100.

Claude

The electricity accrual holds too much. Last month's estimate of $2,040 did not reverse on 1 September:

Accrued expenses, electricity
Opening balance, 31 Aug$2,040.00
+ September accrual$2,100.00
− Reversal of August, not posted$0.00
= Closing balance$4,140.00
− Proposed correction$2,040.00
= Closing after the correction$2,100.00
Expected: this month's accrual$2,100.00

The real August bill of $2,170 went straight to Utilities expense on 9 September. Without the correction, September carries $4,270 of electricity. With it, September carries $2,230.

Claude

Two customers paid in advance. Pinnacle Clinics paid $36,000 on 1 September, and all of it went to Revenue. I move the unearned part to Deferred revenue. I do not enter the receipt again.
